Welcome — I'm here to coach you and your team through your improvement project step by step, so you don't need to be an expert. We'll work through five phases together:
• Define — pin down the problem and who's solving it
• Measure — get the real numbers
• Analyse — find the true root cause
• Improve — test and apply the fix
• Control — make the gains stick
Right now we're in Define — the most important phase, because a clear problem is half the solution. For each of the thirteen parts I'll explain what it is and why it matters, show you a finished example, then ask for yours. When all thirteen are agreed, you and your team review the Define report and approve it.

Now let’s move on to baseline_estimate — this is where we define the primary metric that measures the defect your project is solving. It’s vital because this metric is how the project’s success will be judged. If you don’t set it clearly now, later phases won’t be able to compare against it.

A metric is something you can count the same way twice. For example, 'invoice quality' isn’t a metric because two people might score it differently. 'The share of invoices returned by collections for correction' is a metric because you can point at any invoice and say yes or no.

Here’s why it matters: This is the number your whole project is judged on. Define sets it, Measure proves it, Control compares against it. If the definition shifts between phases, nothing downstream compares.

A usable Define baseline has three parts: a number, the period it covers, and where it came from — a report, a log, a sample. 'About 12%' is a start; '12% of invoices returned, January to June, from the collections log' is something we can go and check.

sections.problem_statement: From January to June 2026, 23% of supplier invoices across our three hospital sites were paid after their 30-day terms. Late payments cause suppliers to chase us by phone and email, and some put us on stop — delaying stock for ward managers and costing us interest, lost discounts, and supplier trust. The problem shows at the 'resolve mismatches' and 'approve invoice' steps, where invoices wait.
sections.objective: Reduce the late payment rate from 23% to under 5% by 31 March 2027, and keep it under 5% for three months after that.

scope.out_scope: non-PO invoices, payroll, procurement tendering, and the ERP system itself
